transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-08-28 | Start: 15:00 UTC | Duration: ~58m
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Diego Alvarez (Redwood SE), Jordan Park (Redwood CSM), Priya Rao (Redwood Solutions), Liam O'Connell (Harrow Head of Security), Rana Kapoor (Platform Engineer), Sofia Mendes (App Dev Lead), Tom Brett (IT Ops)
Links/Artifacts referenced: Redwood SSO quickstart (link shared), SOC2 summary doc (link), sample SCIM mapping spreadsheet (to be sent), network pilot runbook (to be scheduled)

[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining — quick roll call, then we'll jump into SSO and RBAC. Hi Liam?
[00:06] Liam: Hi, yes thanks. Ran a quick check, we need to confirm EU-only data residency for this pilot, so that drives some of the questions.
[00:12] Diego: Noted. We'll flag region-specific endpoints and KMS options.
[00:16] Rana: Also want to understand SCIM group sync — we have nested groups and would like mapping to roles in Redwood.
[00:22] Maya: Perfect. Agenda: quick SAML setup, SCIM provisioning, RBAC/least-privilege pattern, then audit logs + KMS.
[00:30] [00:30] Diego: I'll start with SAML — typical flow is IdP -> Redwood SP; we publish SP metadata including ACS URL and entity ID. On your side you need to set up a relying party. Common gotcha is clock skew for assertion validity, so NTP sync matters.
[01:05] Liam: For assertions, do you support encrypted assertions or only signed? We need assertion encryption for compliance.
[01:12] Diego: We support signed assertions and can accept encrypted assertions. There is a small config step; we'll include a sample metadata that includes the encryption cert block.
[01:25] Sofia: And does the SP initiate or are you IdP-initiated for SSO? We already have some IdP-initiated flows in prod.
[01:31] Diego: Both. We can handle IdP-initiated and SP-initiated. For IdP-initiated, make sure the NameID format matches your IdP mapping (email vs persistent).
[01:46] [01:46] Rana: SCIM — we use Okta and Azure AD. Do you support incremental delta syncs vs full sync?
[01:52] Diego: Yes we support SCIM 2.0 with delta syncs and we honor group membership changes. One limitation: group nesting is flattened in our current sync; we can map nested groups to single role but not preserve hierarchy. If nested semantics are needed we can discuss a small mapping layer.
[02:20] Tom: How are service accounts handled? We want machine identities with minimal scope.
[02:26] Maya: Good question — Redwood supports service accounts and API keys with scoped permissions. SEs usually recommend ephemeral tokens for long-running agent processes but we can also issue fine-grained API keys tied to a role.
[02:40] Diego: To expand on roles: typical RBAC model we see is Org Admin, Billing Admin, App Developer, Reader, and Service Principal (machine). Each maps to a set of permissions and allowed routes. You can configure custom roles as well.
[02:58] Liam: For least privilege, how granular is permissioning? Can we restrict models or routes per role?
[03:04] Diego: Yes, you can restrict by model family, by environment (prod vs staging), and by named routes. We also support route-level quotas. It isn't per-parameter level but covers access surfaces.
[03:20] [03:20] Sofia: Any support for Just-in-Time access or approval flows? We have a process to allow elevated access for debugging only after approval.
[03:26] Jordan: We have an integration pattern with your ticketing/approval flow; we also support time-bound role assignments and can automate revocation after a TTL. For full JIT with approval we typically rely on an external PAM or workflow system integrated via SCIM/group changes or API.
[03:48] Liam: Audit logs — retention and export options? We need 7 years for certain records and streaming to Splunk for SOC artifacting.
[03:56] Diego: Audit logs include auth events, model invocations (metadata only — not raw PII by default), role changes, and admin actions. We offer configurable retention (30d, 90d, 365d) on hosted tiers; for longer retention we push logs to customer SIEM via secure syslog/HTTPS. For EU residency we can keep logs in-region.
[04:26] Rana: Are logs end-to-end encrypted in transit? We want TLS and client cert auth.
[04:31] Diego: Yes TLS 1.2/1.3; we support mutual TLS to SIEM endpoints for log shipping.
[04:38] [04:38] Tom: KMS / CMEK — can we bring our own keys (AWS KMS / GCP KMS)?
[04:45] Maya: Yes, for the Private and Dedicated configurations we support CMEK with AWS KMS & GCP KMS. On Hosted we offer customer-managed keys for certain enterprise tiers — we'll confirm exact artifact requirements.
[04:58] Liam: Key rotation and access controls — do you store plaintext keys?
[05:03] Diego: We never store plaintext keys. We use envelope encryption; only wrapped keys are stored. Key operations are proxied to the KMS. Rotation is supported; we keep rotation events in audit logs.
[05:20] [05:20] Sofia: Data residency — can you guarantee EU-only processing and storage for model cache and logs?
[05:27] Maya: Yes, we have EU regions and can pin workload and KV cache to EU. Note: third-party model weights pulled from external registries might need additional controls; we recommend dedicated capacity for strict residency guarantees.
[05:46] Liam: SOC 2 and ISO artifacts — can you provide a SOC 2 Type II and ISO attestation?
[05:52] Jordan: We'll provide redacted SOC 2 Type II reports and our ISO 27001 scope checklist via secure link. We'll also include our control mappings for SSO/SCIM and key management.
[06:10] [06:10] Rana: A technical question — if an assertion is replayed, how do you mitigate?
[06:15] Diego: We check assertion timestamps and nonces; our SP enforces a narrow validity window and rejects stale assertions. Replay protections are in place.
[06:25] Rana: Ok good.
[06:28] [06:28] Maya: Walkthrough of SCIM attribute mapping — Diego?
[06:30] Diego: We'll send a sample CSV with common attributes. Example mapping: scim:userName -> email, scim:name.givenName -> firstName, scim:name.familyName -> lastName, scim:groups -> role. For delta sync we'll surface operation types (add, remove, replace) and an audit trail.
[07:00] [07:00] Sofia: How about groups that map to multiple roles? e.g., analytics-read maps to Reader and a custom rate limit?
[07:06] Diego: We support composite mapping: a group can map to multiple role bindings; rate limits are policy attributes attached to bindings. We'll include examples in the mapping doc.
[07:24] Liam: Does Redwood persist user content in logs or only metadata? This is a compliance question.
[07:30] Diego: By default we persist metadata about requests (model, token count, latency, user ID hash) and redact user-generated PII from logs unless you opt-in for debug logging. For customers with strict controls we recommend no payload retention and log forwarding to your SIEM.
[07:56] [07:56] Tom: Network: will we need to open ranges outbound? We prefer egress restrictions.
[08:02] Maya: For hosted mode there's a set of known egress IP ranges; for dedicated/private we can establish VPC peering or private connectivity. We'll share the pilot runbook to scope firewall rules.
[08:18] Rana: Any gotchas for Okta SCIM mapping for nested groups?
[08:23] Diego: Okta often represents nested groups with a single groupId membership; our mapping flattens; for hierarchical semantics you might want to push a flattened view or implement a small lambda that translates nested to role sets before provisioning.
[08:44] [08:44] Sofia: Encryption at rest specifics? AES-256?
[08:47] Diego: AES-256 envelope encryption, keys in KMS. For in-transit TLS; for logs we support client cert mTLS to SIEMs.
[08:56] Liam: Anything about breach notification SLAs?
[09:00] Jordan: Our standard enterprise contract includes incident notification timelines (72 hours for confirmed breaches) and we have an incident response playbook we can share.
[09:12] [09:12] Maya: Recap — we'll share SAML metadata, SCIM mapping examples, SOC artifacts, and KMS/CMEK implementation notes. Pilot connectivity scheduled next week tentatively.
[09:24] Liam: Sounds good. One more: can we have an audit trail of role elevation approvals?
[09:30] Diego: Yes, we can surface role-change events with approver metadata in audit logs; if you need a formal approval chain we usually integrate with your ticketing system.
[09:45] [09:45] Tom: I'll compile firewall rules and SIEM collector endpoint and send to Maya.
[09:50] Maya: Thanks all, we'll follow up with the artifacts.
[09:56] Jordan: I'll drop the SOC2 redacted link to the thread.
[09:59] End.

Transcript notes: occasional transcription artifacts — speaker overlap was present between Maya and Diego around 02:20; some proper nouns (e.g., KMS provider names) may be slightly garbled in auto transcription. References to docs are represented as notes/links rather than full attachments.
pm_notes: Customer is enterprise-sized analytics firm with strict EU residency and SOC 2 needs; prime candidate for Dedicated offering or Hosted with CMEK+region pinning. Risk: nested group semantics; workaround requires light integration work or a mapping lambda. Proposed pilot to validate SCIM and log shipping.
